title: Production blueprint
description: The input to production, and the only place a proof's structure is decided. `generate_wit.py` renders this and invents nothing — so every property the artifact must have is a property this file must have, and until now those properties were enforced by ad-hoc code inside the renderer with no schema anyone could read. A contract that lives only in the checker is a contract nobody can satisfy on purpose.

name.description: Becomes the MODULE and THEOREM label. Lowercase, underscores; it ends up in a Lean identifier.

claim.description: The informal statement, verbatim. Its hash IS the frozen target, so a change here is a different claim rather than an edit to this one.

formal_statement.description: The Lean signature, supplied and never guessed. Autoformalization is where fidelity is lost, and a guessed statement type-checks exactly as well as a right one.

preamble.description: Imports and options. Kept out of `formal_statement` so the fidelity gate is not diffing an import list against a claim.

statement_tampering_forbidden.description: Literally true. A blueprint that does not assert this is not asking for a protected run.

frozen_target_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the normalized claim. The renderer recomputes it and refuses when they differ, which is the check that stops a plan drifting from the thing it was approved for.

external_dependencies.description: Every result the plan may cite. A step citing anything outside this list is refused: out of scope is not a step.

lemma_plan.description: The proof structure. Each entry becomes one WIT step and one Lean obligation, so a plan of one step has decomposed nothing and will fail the sketch rubric for exactly that reason.

depends_on.description: Earlier steps only. WIT forbids forward references, and so does the renderer.

formalization.description: The Lean proposition and tactic for this step. A step without one keeps its hole, and the artifact is honestly incomplete rather than confidently wrong.

status_to_assert.description: What the artifact may claim about itself. VERIFIED is absent from this enum by design: a blueprint is structurally incapable of ordering a success claim, because the thing that grants success has to be able to refuse.
